sources.entry: yarn.social - Self-Hosted, Twitter™-like Decentralised micro-logging platform. No ads, no tracking, your content, your data. (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.name: yarn
summary.one_liner: Yarn (yarn.social) is a self-hosted, Twitter-like decentralised micro-blogging platform written in Go, with a server (yarnd) and a command-line client (yarnc).
use_cases: host a community social feed for a group
post and read timelines from the terminal
self-host a social network without ads or tracking
summary.what_it_does: Yarn is a self-hosted, Twitter-like micro-blogging platform. The server binary yarnd runs a "pod" that serves a built-in web interface and an API. The command-line client yarnc can log in to a pod, show a timeline, make posts and parse/analyse twtxt feeds. Pods can be installed from prebuilt binaries, Homebrew, or built from Go source, and deployed with Docker, Docker Swarm or as a standalone binary. Configuration is via command-line flags and environment variables, including secrets for production use and SMTP settings for email.
notable: Uses the twtxt feed format for decentralised interoperation
Ships a command-line client (yarnc) and an official Go client library
Docker images published for AMD64 and ARM64
caveats: Registrations are disabled by default and must be enabled with the -R flag
Media upload features require ffmpeg and its dev packages to be installed when building from source
The public demo instance is deliberately locked down, so some functionality is restricted
The twt.js JavaScript client is described as old and unmaintained
